Rashi on Sotah 13b:11:1.hebrew: שהוריד אצטגניני פרעה מגדולתן - כשפתר את החלום, והם לא ידעו לפותרו:
Rashi on Sotah 13b:11:1.english: That he brought down the astrologers of Pharaoh from their greatness - When he interpreted the dream, and they did not know how to interpret it.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:12:1.english: For himself - For homosexual intercourse, because of his beauty.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:12:3.english: Gabriel came and castrated him - [Rashi] did not have this in the text.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:13:1.hebrew: ברב בישר - את בני מחלקותו: "רב לכם בני לוי". והקב"ה מדקדק עם הצדיקים כחוט השערה, ונענש באותה מדה:
Rashi on Sotah 13b:13:1.english: With "rav" he announced - to the members of his dispute [Korach's company], "It is too much for you [rav lachem], sons of Levi." And the Holy One, blessed be He, is exacting with the righteous to a hair's breadth, and [Moses] was punished with the same measure.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:14:1.hebrew: רב יש לך - הגיע מלכותו של יהושע, ואין לך מלכות נוגעת בחבירתה:
Rashi on Sotah 13b:14:1.english: You have much [rav yesh lakh] - The reign of Joshua has arrived, and there is no kingdom that overlaps with another.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:15:1.hebrew: ד"א רב לך - די לך, אל תרבה בבקשה, שלא יאמרו: הרב כמה קשה, שאינו שומע לתלמיד, ותלמיד כמה סרבן מפציר. ולשון חכמים הוא כך: היו מסרבין בו לישא את בת אחותו (בנדרים (ד' סג:)), היו מסרבין בו שיאכל עמו (בשבועות (דף כג:)):
Rashi on Sotah 13b:15:1.english: Another explanation: "It is enough for you" - It is enough for you; do not increase your request, so that they will not say: How harsh the master is, that he does not listen to the student, and how insistent and importunate the student is! And this is a expression of the Sages, [as in]: "They would press him to marry his sister's daughter" (in Nedarim (63b)); "They would press him to eat with him" (in Shevuot (23b)).

Rashi on Sotah 13b:15:2.hebrew: לפום גמלא שיחנא - לפי כח הגמל מרבין במשאו, אף כאן לפי צדקתו מדקדק אחריו:
Rashi on Sotah 13b:15:2.english: According to the camel, [so is] the load - According to the strength of the camel, they increase its burden; here too, according to a person's righteousness, [God] is more exacting with him.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:16:1.english: Today [my years] were completed - On this day I was born.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:17:1.hebrew: לא נס ליחה - לא ברח לחלוחית כחו:
Rashi on Sotah 13b:17:1.english: His moisture had not fled - The moisture of his strength had not fled.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:19:1.hebrew: דיו זוגי - שני זוגות, שני חבירים היו: בהתחלת היום למשה, וסופו ליהושע:
Rashi on Sotah 13b:19:1.english: Dio zugi - Two pairs; there were two companions: the beginning of the day was Moses's, and its end was Joshua's.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:1:1.hebrew: קיים זה מה שכתוב בזה - אגדה זו מפורשת במכילתא בפרשת ויהי בשלח פרעה: כתיב בזה אנכי, וכתיב בזה התחת אלהים אנכי; כתיב בזה לא יהיה לך, וכתיב בזה האלהים אני ירא; לא תשא, חי פרעה; זכור את יום השבת, וטבוח טבח והכן — ואין זה אלא יום השבת, וכן הוא אומר: והכינו את אשר יביאו. וכן כל עשרת הדברות: לא תשנא את אחיך בלבבך, לא תקום ולא תטור, וחי אחיך עמך:
Rashi on Sotah 13b:1:1.english: This one fulfilled what is written in that one - This aggadah is explained in the Mekhilta, in the portion "And it was when Pharaoh sent [the people out]" (Beshalach). It is written in this one [the Ark of the Torah, i.e., the Ten Commandments], "I am [the Lord your God]," and it is written in this one [Joseph's words], "Am I in place of God?" It is written in this one, "You shall have no [other gods] before Me," and it is written in this one, "I fear God." [In this one it is written] "You shall not take [the name of the Lord your God in vain]," [and in this one], "By the life of Pharaoh." [In this one it is written] "Remember the Sabbath day," [and in this one], "slaughter an animal and prepare" (Genesis 43:16) — and this refers only to the Sabbath day [i.e., the preparation for it], and so it says, "and they shall prepare what they bring" (Exodus 16:5). And so too for all of the Ten Commandments: [it is written in this one] "You shall not hate your brother in your heart," "You shall not take vengeance and you shall not bear a grudge," and [in this one] "and your brother shall live with you."

Rashi on Sotah 13b:23:1.english: In the wings of the Shechinah - In the corner of the garment of His glory.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:23:2.english: Who will rise up for me against evildoers - To rebuke them for My sake.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:24:1.hebrew: פשר דבר - שהיה יודע לעשות פשרה ביני ובין בני:
Rashi on Sotah 13b:24:1.english: The interpretation of a matter - That he knew how to make a compromise between me and my children.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:24:2.english: Semalyon - The name of a sage.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:26:1.hebrew: סימן בתוך סימן - כלומר, סימנים הרבה: בארץ מואב, בגיא, מול בית פעור, ואעפ"כ לא ידע וגו':
Rashi on Sotah 13b:26:1.english: A sign within a sign - That is, many signs: in the land of Moab, in the valley, opposite Beit Peor; and nevertheless "no man knows [of his burial place]" etc.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:2:1.hebrew: ואי לא איעסק ביה משה וכו' - כלומר, היאך הניחו ישראל למשה להתעסק בו לבדו? וכי לא חשו לשבועה? ואם לא נתעסק בו משה, לא היו הם מתעסקין:
Rashi on Sotah 13b:2:1.english: And if Moshe had not occupied himself with it, etc. - That is to say, how did Israel leave Moshe to occupy himself with it alone? Did they not take the oath into account? And if Moshe had not occupied himself with it, they would not have occupied themselves with it.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:2:2.hebrew: הכתיב וכו' - אלמא, לאחר שנפטר משה בערבות מואב, נתעסקו בהן ישראל, והעבירום את הירדן:
Rashi on Sotah 13b:2:2.english: But isn't it written, etc. - Evidently, after Moses passed away in the plains of Moab, Israel occupied themselves with them [the bones of Joseph], and brought them across the Jordan.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:2:3.hebrew: ותו אי לא הוו מתעסקי ביה ישראל - לאחר שנפטר משה, בניו מי לא הוו מיעסקי ביה? והיאך הניחו בניו את שאר העם להתעסק בו? והכתיב בשכם "ויהיו לבני יוסף לנחלה" וגו', אלמא בנחלתם קברוהו, דחביב היה עליהן:
Rashi on Sotah 13b:2:3.english: And furthermore, if Israel were not occupied with it - After Moses died, were his sons not occupied with it [his burial]? And how did his sons leave the rest of the people to occupy themselves with it? And is it not written regarding Shechem, "and they became the inheritance of the children of Joseph," etc.? Evidently they buried him in their own inheritance, because he was dear to them.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:3:1.hebrew: אמרו - בניו בעצמם הניחו לו, שיתעסקו בו כל ישראל:
Rashi on Sotah 13b:3:1.english: They said - His own sons themselves allowed him [to be treated this way], so that all of Israel would occupy themselves with him.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:3:2.hebrew: כבודו במרובים יותר מבמועטין - וישראל אמרו בעצמם: בעוד משה קיים, הניחו שיתעסק בו משה לבדו. כבודו בגדולים יותר מבקטנים:
Rashi on Sotah 13b:3:2.english: His honor is greater with many than with few - And Israel themselves said: While Moses is still alive, leave it [to him] that Moses alone will occupy himself with it. His honor is greater with the great ones than with the small ones.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:4:1.hebrew: משכם גנבוהו - כדכתיב וישלחהו מעמק חברון ויבא שכמה, ושם היו רועין. ודותן אינה מקום. והאי דכתיב (שם) ויאמר האיש נסעו מזה וגו', כך אמר לו: אתה אומר "את אחי אנכי מבקש" — סעו מן האחוה הזאת, ואין מחזיקין עצמן כאחין לך, כי שמעתי אומרים נלכה ונבקש דתות ודינין, היאך להמיתו אם יבא אצלנו:
Rashi on Sotah 13b:4:1.english: From Shechem they stole him - As it is written, "And he sent him out of the valley of Hebron, and he came to Shechem" (Genesis 37:14), and that is where they were grazing [their flocks]. And "Dothan" is not [the name of] a place. And as for that which is written (there), "And the man said: They have journeyed from here," etc. (Genesis 37:17) — this is what he said to him: You say, "I am seeking my brothers" — journey away from this brotherhood, for they no longer regard themselves as brothers to you; for I heard them saying, "Let us go and seek out pretexts and legal rulings [as to] how to put him to death if he comes to us."

Rashi on Sotah 13b:5:1.hebrew: הכא כתיב ויקח משה - ולא שאר העם:
Rashi on Sotah 13b:5:1.english: Here it is written, "And Moses took" - and not the rest of the people.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:7:1.hebrew: אף מורידין אותו מגדולתו - מן השמים. למתחיל ואינו גומר, אלא אם כן נאנס, כמשה שמת בעבר הירדן:
Rashi on Sotah 13b:7:1.english: Also, they bring him down from his greatness - From Heaven. [This applies] to one who begins [a mitzvah] and does not complete it, unless he was prevented by circumstances beyond his control, like Moses, who died on the other side of the Jordan.

Rashi on Sotah 13b:7:2.hebrew: [וירד יהודה - שהוא התחיל בהצלת יוסף כשאמר "מה בצע", ולא גמר]:
Rashi on Sotah 13b:7:2.english: [And Judah went down - For he began the rescue of Joseph when he said, "What profit is there?" and did not finish it.]

Rashi on Sotah 13b:9:1.hebrew: נקרא יוסף עצמות בחייו - שנאמר "והעליתם את עצמותי מזה", ועודנו חי:
Rashi on Sotah 13b:9:1.english: Joseph was called "bones" during his lifetime - As it is stated: "And you shall bring up my bones from here," while he was still alive.

Tosafot on Sotah 13b:24:1.hebrew: סמליון אומר - פי' ר"ח: אית דאמרי מלאך, ואית דאמרי שם חכם. ערוך:
Tosafot on Sotah 13b:24:1.english: Simlyon says - Rabbeinu Chananel explained: Some say [it is the name of] an angel, and some say [it is] the name of a sage. [So it is cited in the] Arukh.
